name: run_python
description: Run a Python script inside a bubblewrap sandbox to inspect the target binary. The sandbox exposes the target ONLY at /workspace/binary (read-only); /scratch is writable for intermediate dumps (e.g. objdump output); the network is isolated; python3 standard library and binutils (file, readelf, objdump, nm, strings, xxd, od, hexdump, size, c++filt) are available, but NO third-party packages (no capstone/pyelftools -- parse ELF via subprocess to readelf/objdump or struct). Each call returns an observation_id and pending evidence_id(s); after the output has been returned in an earlier response, summarize any evidence you intend to cite.

script.description: Full Python source. Call binutils via subprocess, e.g. subprocess.run(['objdump','-d','-Mintel','/workspace/binary'],capture_output=True,text=True). Return findings on stdout (that becomes your evidence).

timeout_sec.description: Execution timeout in seconds. 0 means default 240.

max_output_chars.description: Cap captured stdout/stderr characters (head+tail). 0 means default 60000.

name: summarize_evidence
description: Write or revise natural-language claims and verification locators for evidence returned by one earlier inspection-tool observation. This tool never creates evidence or changes the Host supporting excerpt, kind, polarity, or provenance. Every evidence item cited by a final verdict must be summarized first.

observation_id.description: The obs_XXXX identifier from the earlier inspection-tool result.

evidence_id.description: An ev_XXXX identifier returned by the specified observation.

claim.description: A concise natural-language statement of what the raw target-binary output establishes.

excerpt.description: One to twelve exact, complete lines copied from the specified observation output for independent verification.

address_ranges.description: Up to four inclusive binary address ranges that locate the claimed behavior. Use an empty array only when the evidence has no meaningful code address.

name: submit_detection_result
description: Submit a patch-presence status using summarized target-binary evidence ids, concise reasoning, and decisive addresses. The Host validates every cited ledger item before writing the artifact.
